web_evidence.title: Narrating Selves amid Library Shelves: Literary Mediation and Demediation in S. by J. J. Abrams and Doug Dorst
web_evidence.note: Peer-reviewed structural analysis establishes that S. consists of Ship of Theseus, Eric and Jen's reciprocal handwritten annotations, and inserted documents, and treats the annotations as epistolary narration. This supports their constitutive narrative status but does not itself explicitly identify both grammatical persons.

web_evidence.title: An Analysis of Cyclicality in the Novels In the Lake of the Woods by Tim O'Brien, S. by Jeffrey Jacob Abrams and Doug Dorst, and Only Revolutions by Mark Z. Danielewski
web_evidence.note: Academic narratological analysis explicitly distinguishes two main stories: the inner Ship of Theseus and an outer novel written through Eric and Jen's first-person conversations in the margins.

web_evidence.title: 'S' — Desktop
web_evidence.note: Doug Dorst explains that he completed Ship of Theseus as a standalone novel and then layered in the marginal notes; this establishes distinct sustained story layers, not their grammatical persons.

web_evidence.title: What I'm Reading: S., J.J. Abrams and Doug Dorst
web_evidence.note: Notre Dame Magazine describes S. as almost two books in one and says Eric and Jen's interactions form their own full-bodied story across hundreds of pages alongside Ship of Theseus. This confirms constitutive scope but not grammatical-person alternation.

person_note: S. contains sustained narration in different persons. The printed inner novel Ship of Theseus repeatedly narrates S. externally as he across extended passages, while Eric and Jen's handwritten exchanges are not incidental dialogue: scholarly evidence identifies them as a constitutive outer epistolary novel, and the supplied passages repeatedly show both participants narrating their own lives as I. One Tier B narratological study explicitly identifies the inner narrator as nonparticipating and third-person and the outer Eric/Jen narration as autodiegetic with first-person pronouns. Sources that mention multiple storylines, perspectives, or epistolarity without naming both persons are retained only as structural context. Rhetorical and generic you passages do not establish second-person narration. The reconciled label is therefore ALTERNATING, with high confidence because diagnostic Goodreads passages and explicit Tier B whole-book analysis independently agree. Audit: independent review retained ALTERNATING/high, preserved constitutive margin correspondence as first-person evidence despite upstream dialogue buckets, narrowed overclaimed web supports, and changed short or contextless he/I passages to unmarked or unclear rather than inheriting the book label.
